skill.name: claude-opus-4-5-migration

content.value_statement: Teams moving from older Claude models must update model strings and tune prompts safely. This skill guides targeted Opus 4.5 migrations for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Identifies supported Sonnet 4.0, Sonnet 4.5, and Opus 4.1 model strings for replacement.
Provides Opus 4.5 identifiers for Anthropic API, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Azure AI Foundry.
Flags the unsupported 1M context beta header during migration.
Guides effort parameter configuration when the user requests it.
Offers conditional prompt adjustments for tool use, scope control, code exploration, design quality, and thinking wording.
limitations: Does not migrate Haiku 4.5 or unrelated model families.
Prompt snippets should be applied only when the user reports a matching issue.
Does not verify current provider availability, pricing, or deployment status.
Requires project-specific testing before production rollout.

use_cases.title: API Migration Review
use_cases.description: Update supported Claude model identifiers across an application before testing Opus 4.5.

use_cases.title: Prompt Behavior Tuning
use_cases.description: Adjust prompts only when Opus 4.5 behavior changes create a clear issue.

use_cases.title: Provider Migration Checklist
use_cases.description: Compare Anthropic API, Bedrock, Vertex AI, and Azure model identifiers during an upgrade.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Model Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Migrate this project from Claude Sonnet 4.5 to Opus 4.5. Update model strings only and summarize each changed file.

prompt_templates.title: Provider-Specific Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate migration across one cloud provider.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this AWS Bedrock Claude integration. Replace supported older model identifiers with the Opus 4.5 Bedrock identifier.

prompt_templates.title: Prompt Issue Adjustment
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt tuning after behavior changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: The migrated agent now calls tools too often. Apply only the relevant Opus 4.5 prompt adjustment and explain the change.

prompt_templates.title: Full Migration Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for a multi-provider codebase.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this codebase for Opus 4.5 migration readiness. Check model strings, unsupported beta headers, effort settings, and prompt behavior risks.

output_examples.input: Migrate a Python service that uses Sonnet 4.5 on the Anthropic API.
output: Updated supported Claude model identifiers to Opus 4.5.
Removed unsupported 1M context beta usage where present.
Provided a short migration summary for review.

output_examples.input: Review an agent prompt after moving from Opus 4.1 to Opus 4.5.
output: Kept model string changes separate from prompt edits.
Applied only the prompt adjustment tied to the reported behavior.
Listed testing areas for tool calls, scope control, and response wording.

best_practices: Start with model string changes before changing prompt behavior.
Apply prompt snippets only for a reported issue or explicit user request.
Test each provider integration after updating identifiers and beta headers.
anti_patterns: Do not migrate Haiku models with this skill.
Do not append every prompt snippet without a matching problem.
Do not assume provider availability without checking your deployment environment.

faq.question: Does this skill migrate Haiku models?
faq.answer: No. It explicitly excludes Haiku 4.5 and unrelated model families.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it rewrite prompts automatically?
faq.answer: No. It applies prompt changes only when the user asks or reports a matching behavior issue.

faq.question: Does it make network calls?
faq.answer: No evidence found in the audited files. The skill is documentation and prompt guidance only.

faq.question: Can it update cloud provider identifiers?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes identifiers for Anthropic API, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Azure AI Foundry.

faq.question: Should every workload use high effort?
faq.answer: No. High effort is recommended for best performance, while medium or low effort can reduce cost and latency.
